mostWorthwhile.text: Trapping particles and then moving the mucus toward the throat made the relationship between mucus and cilia clear. The planned pictures show both the trapped material and the direction of movement.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the moving lining to the body felt like an extra assembly step rather than a new biological mechanism, although it placed the defense in the whole-body model.

surprise.text: My attempt to combine the lining directly with macrophages instead connected the lining to the body automatically. The earlier picture also showed that some particles escape the mucus and reach the air sacs.

arbitrary.text: The required body connection before adding macrophages was not obvious to me; the compatibility feedback resolved it, but I had expected the two defenses to combine directly.

continue.text: I would consider continuing: the complementary defenses and their limitations were interesting, though the largely predictable assembly offered few meaningful choices. The macrophage picture and explanation show engulfment, but do not explain how recognition works in detail.
